message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face down as the draw pile.
• Turn over the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card (Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild, or Wild Draw Four), follow its effect immediately. | • The first player is the one to the left of the dealer. | | **2. Turn Order** | • Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a Reverse is played).
• On your turn, you may play **one** card from your hand that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top card on the discard pile. | • If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile. | | **3. Drawing** | • If you draw a card that can be played immediately, you may do so on the same turn. Otherwise, your turn ends. | • If the draw pile runs out, reshuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new draw pile. | | **4. Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Turns the direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | • Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card. If challenged and you had a playable card, you must draw six cards. | | **5. Winning a Round** | • The round ends when a player discards all their cards.
• That player scores points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands:
 • Number cards = face value.
 • Draw Two, Skip, Reverse = 20 points.
 • Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | • The first player to reach 500 points wins the game. | | **6. Optional House Rules** | • “Uno” shout: When you have one card left, you must say “Uno!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to do so results in drawing two penalty cards.
• “Stacking” – Some groups allow stacking Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards. | • Clarify house rules before starting. | **Quick Tips** - Keep track of the current color and number to anticipate opponents’ moves. - Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. - Pay attention to the “Uno” shout rule—missing it can cost you extra cards. Enjoy playing Uno!
